Export a region¶

The export window writes a time range of the file, and as an option a frequency band, to a new SigMF or raw file.

Open the export window¶

Do one of these steps:

  • Select File → Export region….

  • Press Ctrl+E.

  • Right-click the waterfall (do not drag). Then select Select a region to export…, Export this view… or Export the channel….

Select the region¶

Fill from sets the region from one of these sources:

Source

Time range

Band

View

The view

The full band

Channel

The view

The band of the channel filter

Markers

The time markers

The frequency markers

Select…

The box that you drag on the waterfall

The box that you drag on the waterfall

You can also type or adjust each value. The start and the end are in seconds or in samples. The band is a low and a high frequency, or a center frequency and a width.

To select a box on the waterfall:

  1. Click Select…, or right-click the waterfall and select Select a region to export….

  2. Drag a box with the left mouse button. The view does not pan while you drag.

  3. To cancel, press Esc.

A right-drag still zooms to a box.

While the export window is open, the waterfall shows the region:

  • To move the region, drag the box.

  • To change its size, drag its edges or corners.

  • A full-band region shows as two time lines.

  • The I/Q, AM, FM and PM plots show the time range as a shaded area.

Full band or a band¶

Full band: wvt copies the samples without a change. The output has the same format, rate and center frequency as the source. If the source is big-endian or has I and Q swapped, wvt writes the output in the standard order.

A band: wvt makes a new recording of the band only. The window shows the output rate, center frequency, taps, decimation, size and file name before you export. The output format is one of:

  • cf32.

  • ci16, at half the size. wvt clips values above full scale and shows the number of clipped samples.

Write the file¶

  1. Make sure that the file name and the format are correct.

  2. Click Export.

The export runs in the background with a progress bar.

  • Cancel stops the export and deletes the partial file.

  • If the file exists, wvt replaces it only after you confirm.

  • wvt checks the free disk space before it starts.

  • The export stays in the loaded segment.

The default name carries the rate and the frequency, for example capture_12.5s_100.3MHz_200kSps. Thus a raw export opens in wvt without options.

Metadata¶

The SigMF metadata of the output has:

  • The sample rate and the center frequency.

  • core:datetime: the start time of the source plus the start of the range, if the source has a start time.

  • A wvt:extract object with the source file, the sample range, the band and the filter.

Command line¶

Option

Function

--extract-out PATH

Write the region to PATH (without the extension), then stop

--extract T0:T1

The time range in seconds. The default is the full segment

--extract-band LO:HI

Only this band, in absolute Hz. Without this option, wvt copies the samples

--extract-format cf32|ci16

The output format for a band. The default is cf32

--extract-overwrite

Replace output files that exist

--export-window

Open the export window with the --chan band, or with the view

--segment limits the export. --record-format sigmf|raw sets the file type.

wvt cap.sigmf-meta --extract 10:20 --extract-out part                               # 10 s, copied
wvt cap.sigmf-meta --extract 10:20 --extract-band 100.2M:100.4M --extract-out fm    # a 200 kHz band

How it works¶

For a band, wvt does these steps:

  1. It mixes the center of the band to 0 Hz.

  2. It applies a low-pass FIR filter. The passband is the band, flat to the edges. Each side has a 25 % transition band. The stopband is approximately 74 dB down.

  3. It decimates to fs / D, where D = ⌊fs / (1.25 · BW)⌋.

If a GPU is available, the filter runs on the GPU. The mixer phase is a function of the absolute sample number. The self-check build/extract_check tests the copies, the band filter, the metadata, the input checks and the cancel.

For the design, refer to the region export design record.
